chunks: From him, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said:

I read in a letter from 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): Our companions differed in their narrations from Abu 'Abdullah (peace be upon him) regarding the two rak'ahs of Fajr during travel. Some of them narrated: 'Pray them in the saddle (mount),' and some of them narred: 'Do not pray them except on the ground.' So inform me of what you do, so that I may follow your example in that. And he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'You are given leeway; whichever you do is acceptable.'

key_terms.رَكْعَتَيِ الْفَجْرِ: The two voluntary rak'ahs of Fajr prayer

ai.seo_question: How should one pray the two rak'ahs of Fajr while traveling according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the scholarly nuance in Shia jurisprudence regarding the voluntary two-rak'ahs of Fajr during travel, resolving the apparent contradiction between praying on the mount versus on the ground. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the principle of *tawassu'* (flexibility), indicating that both practices are valid and the choice depends on individual ease, thereby preventing unnecessary rigidity in religious practice. This reflects the broader Shia legal methodology of accommodating varying conditions without declaring one method superior to the other when both are rooted in prophetic tradition.
